item.title: Austin Championship: Trace Crowe grabs 54-hole lead late
item.description: Trace Crowe birdied his final two holes Saturday to get to 14 under and separate himself from three other players through 54 holes of the inaugural Austin Championship . Chad Ramey, Erik van Rooyen and Sami Valimaki all could have shared the lead heading into Sunday's final round at Fazio Canyons Golf Course if Crowe had faltered down the stretch. But the 30-year-old Crowe, who is seeking his first win on Tour this week in Texas, birdied the par-3 17th and followed it up with another circle at No. 18 as part of the final grouping on the course. "It was like 220 straight into the wind, I was just trying to hit a 4-iron as low as I could and push it just a touch," Crowe recalled. "It was actually a pretty good shot to end up in that bunker, it was a good leave. He called the lie perfect as it was just sitting uphill. "It just came out perfect and went in — me and my caddie both had a feeling I was going to make that before we got it, so it was pretty cool to see that go in," he added. Heavy winds began to impact players still on their back nines Saturday afternoon, and Crowe was no exception. After setting the course record on Thursday with an opening-round 62, Crowe bogeyed the first two holes on his back nine on Moving Day. Another square at the par-4 16th put his chances in doubt but the run of birdies at the end of his round vaulted him ahead for the solo lead. Americans Ben Kohles and Max Greyserman are two back of Crowe's lead, while eight players sit T-7 at 11 under. Ramey had the clubhouse lead for more than an hour. He got there by limiting mistakes — the 34-year-old Mississippi State alum has posted just three bogeys, one in each round. Saturday's error came at the par-3 17th, the same hole Crowe birdied from an hour later. "On a week like this to kind of finally get some good results and be in a good position going into Sunday, it's great to see," said Ramey, who entered the week No. 136 in the FedExCup Fall standings and has moved up to a projected No. 68. Austin Championship - Final Rd The Austin Championship tees off at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa in Austin, Texas. That would give Ramey a card for 2027, despite not having a top 10 finish in his first 26 starts. Valimaki, who won for the first time at the RSM Classic last November , moved into the co-leader position with a 3-under 69. He opened the inaugural tournament 68-66 after making his first PGA Tour start since July at last week's WWT Championship. "It was good to take some time off, it's actually been a long time since I felt like I could enjoy the golf course and I feel like that's the biggest key for me," said Valimaki, who battled a right wrist injury and also received stiches in his left hand. The Finnish player was No. 172 entering the week but has crept up to No. 129 with 18 holes left. item.title: Smyth scores 55-yard field goal in Saints defeat
item.description: Smyth was making his second NFL appearance of the season against the Panthers [Getty Images] Kicker Charlie Smyth landed a late 55-yard field goal, but it wasn't enough to stop New Orleans Saints falling to a 20-17 defeat against Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The former Gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in County Down, was making his second NFL appearance of the season after being elevated from the practice squad for a second successive week. The 25-year-old helped the Saints to an overtime win against Cleveland Browns last weekend with three field goals and two extra points and he was almost the hero again against the Panthers. Smyth, who also kicked two extra points, landed a 55-yard field goal with just 41 seconds left in regulation time to tie the game at 17-17. However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young's drive set up Panthers' kicker Ryan Fitzgerald to score a 54-yard field goal on the final play to win the game.

item.title: ‘Hitting the Powerball’… Kansas City Chiefs star has never had it so good, says Ryan Clark
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs’ newest receiving weapon showed up immediately against the Atlanta Falcons. Chiefs general manager Brett Veach provided a surprise for quarterback Patrick Mahomes at the NFL trade deadline, agreeing a trade for Josh Downs. Downs was traded away by the Indianapolis Colts to the Chiefs for a fourth and fifth round pick, a move that could end up looking like a bargain. The new Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver made an instant impact in Week 10 in his first game for his new team. Downs caught his first touchdown from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter, catching an 18-yard pass in the endzone. NFL expert Ryan Clark reacted to Downs’ first Chiefs touchdown by reflecting on the incredible turnaround in fortunes for the receiver – after leaving the 2-7 Colts. Clark posted on social media: “Man, imagine going to sleep one week with Daniel Jones as your QB, and waking up the next with Patrick Mahomes! “That’s the football version of hitting the Powerball! I know Josh Downs feels like a new man!” Downs leaves a losing team for a winning team Josh Downs had requested a trade away from the Indianapolis Colts after their poor start to the season, and clear intention to rebuild. His Colts team were 2-7 heading into Week 10, while the Chiefs were 6-2 prior to their win over the Falcons. Downs has never played a game in the NFL Playoffs during his three seasons in Indianapolis. Now providing he can stay injury-free in Kansas City, Downs will likely finally get the chance to play in the postseason with the Chiefs. It’s hard to disagree with Ryan Clark’s assessment that he has ‘won the Powerball’ with the trade. item.title: Inside New Chiefs Acquisition Josh Downs’ Debut Vs. Falcons
item.description: Josh Downs of the Kansas City Chiefs makes a catch for a touchdown against Billy Bowman Jr. (No. 33) of the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Nov. 15, 2026. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs wasted no time in unwrapping their new toy. Wide receiver Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired from the Indianapolis Colts for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks on Tuesday, was involved early in Sunday’s 35-13 victory at the Atlanta Falcons. Downs, who had four catches for 51 yards and a touchdown, played in every drive of the first quarter, but it was on special teams where he first saw action. After the Falcons went three-and-out on the game’s opening series, Downs was back to return the punt, though it ended up being a touchback. He was the returner on all three of the Chiefs’ punt returns. In the second quarter, Downs really picked up steam on the offensive side. On the Chiefs’ last drive of the first half, Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker kicked a 41-yard field goal, but the Falcons jumped offside on fourth down, giving the Chiefs a first down and another offensive opportunity. It turned out to be a costly mistake for the Falcons, which would change the game. Lined up with two other wide receivers on the left side, Downs ran an option route, which is one of his specialties, and Patrick Mahomes showed faith in him despite double coverage from defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and C.J. Henderson. The result was an 18-yard touchdown . “That’s a trust play,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said. Two offensive plays before his first touchdown as a Chiefs player, Downs was targeted on consecutive plays, which resulted in a 13-yard catch and then an incompletion. Downs’ lone downside — lame pun intended — came on the Chiefs’ second punt return when he fumbled the 50-yard punt, forcing the Chiefs to start their possession on their own four-yard line. The Chiefs did have some special teams gaffes, including allowing an onside kick to be converted, but Downs was part of a prolific, downfield Chiefs passing game. Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns. “Pat had a huge day,” Reid said, “and was slinging it.” Backup wide receiver Andrew Armstrong scored a 43-yard touchdown on 3rd and 1. Mahomes connected with receiver Rashee Rice who had a 50-yard contested catch for the longest gain of the game. Rice and Downs have their own connection, having trained together in the offseason and coming out of college. “That’s my dog,” Downs said. The Chiefs knew they were getting a dog in Downs after seeing him lead the Colts with seven catches for 72 yards during the Colts’ overtime loss to Kansas City in Week Two. “We saw that firsthand,” Reid said. “I had to watch him live, which wasn’t good.” Further confirmation came from conversations with Chris Ballard, who the Colts fired as general manager earlier this year. item.title: Chiefs thrash Falcons as Mahomes throws five touchdowns
item.description: Patrick Mahomes was back to his imperious best, completing 22-of 35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack in a win that took the Kansas City Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos top of the AFC West (Todd Kirkland) Patrick Mahomes threw for five touchdowns and 348 yards as the Kansas City Chiefs thrashed the Falcons 35-13 at Atlanta on Sunday. Mahomes was back to his imperious best, completing 22-of-35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack in a win that took the Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos top of the AFC West. Rookie Emmett Johnson twice found the end zone, while Josh Downs had a touchdown on his Kansas City debut following a deadline day trade from Indianapolis. Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each scored their first Chiefs touchdowns, grabbing passes of 39 yards and 43 yards respectively as Mahomes dominated the Falcons defense. It was the three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback's most impressive showing since his nine-month injury absence after tearing his knee ligaments last December. "Guys made plays, you know? I gave them chances downfield, and they went out there and made plays happen," said Mahomes. Johnson -- stepping up for Kenneth Walker III, who was absent with a groin injury -- also led the Chiefs' running game, with 22 carries for 101 yards. Star tight end Travis Kelce left the field early, injuring his ankle as he was tackled taking his first catch, but returned in the second quarter. "I thought we did a great job picking up, obviously Kenneth not being here. I thought Emmett did a great job, and then the O-line gave me chances to throw the ball down the field," said Mahomes. It was another miserable day for the Falcons, who trailed 28-3 before Bijan Robinson's fourth-quarter touchdown, and have now lost three straight and five of their past six. Elsewhere, the Cleveland Browns rallied from 17-0 down to stun the Houston Texans 27-24, as Quinshon Judkins ran in a touchdown with less than a minute remaining. The Texans had led with C.J. Stroud's first-half passing touchdowns to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson. The Browns fought back to take the lead with touchdowns either side of halftime, from a Deshaun Watson six-yard run, a KC Concepcion rushing touchdown and two field goals, all without reply. The Texans thought they had salvaged the win with a Stroud pass to Dalton Schultz, before Watson led yet another late game-winning drive and Judkins ran five yards for the win with 53 seconds left. item.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
item.description: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva celebrates victory over Elina Svitolina in the WTA Finals in Indian Wells (MATTHEW STOCKMAN) Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday. Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California. Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament. She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut. "It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva. The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success. "I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself." A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead. Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2. Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead. There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up. She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40. A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5. The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up. The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies. Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1. Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead. The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down. A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40. Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win. Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance. "After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all." rcw/amz

item.title: Cucurella and Huijsen feature as Spain surrender Nations League group lead to England
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 15: Jude Bellingham of England gestures towards Marc Cucurella of Spain during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Spain and England at Riyadh Air Metropolitano on November 15, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a party atmosphere at a sold-out Metropolitano on Sunday night as Spain hosted England in their first game in the Spanish capital since conquering the World Cup in the summer. Luis de la Fuente’s side had won five from five in the UEFA Nations League campaign and were unbeaten in 90 minutes in 43 games, since March 2024, with this expected to see them crowned as group winners in the UEFA Nations League. Instead, England ran out the winners, taking a 3-0 lead through a Harry Kane penalty, an Ezri Konsa header and a third from Ben White. Spain did battle back to 3-2 after the Three Lions went down to 10 men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the box, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the resulting penalty and Nico Williams adding another. At left-back, Marc Cucurella had a night to forget. Booked for a foul on Morgan Rogers early in the second half, he won only one of five ground duels and didn’t complete any tackles as he struggled with the threat of Rogers down England’s right flank. Going forwards, he also contributed little with only two passes into the final third and failing to find his target with his only attempted cross. In the second half, he was joined by Dean Huijsen, who came on at the break to replace Pau Cubarsí, who conceded the penalty which gave England the lead before half-time. Huijsen too found it hard going up against Kane, losing all four of his aerial duels, and also failing to complete any tackles. Where he did contribute more was in Spain’s more direct approach with Huijsen often carrying the ball forwards before launching it into the final third later on, registering six passes into the final third and a step by 92% pass accuracy overall. Spain have now finished second in the group, behind England on goal difference, which means that they will face a tougher draw in the Nations League play-off before a final four.

item.title: The full Division III football bracket, along with at least 1 major snub
item.description: The transition from a selection committee to the NCAA Power Index (NPI) has taken some of the guess work from the Division III football championship bracket. The expansion from 32 teams to 40 has ensured fewer snubs. But that doesn't mean this year's field doesn't bring surprises. Geographic limitations and the NPI's difference of opinion with the D3Football.com rankings means there's plenty to quibble about with this year's schedule. Wheaton College, the first team to beat powerhouse North Central in the regular season since 2019, went from the poll's No. 1 team to the bracket's third overall seed. Wisconsin-Whitewater, chasing its first national title since 2014, will have home field advantage all the way to the national championship game in Salem, Virginia after topping out the NPI formula. Teams with solid resumes, like Bethel and reigning national champion Wisconsin-River Falls, were left out. The New England Small College Athletic Conference (NESCAC) put three teams in the bracket even though the league didn't play a single out-of-conference game . North Central and DePauw, each ranked in the poll's top 15, will face off in a second round game that ensures at least one realistic title contender will be gone before the field is whittled down to 16 teams. item.title: When Arsenal Witnessed Dixie Dean Make Football History
item.description: When Arsenal Witnessed Dixie Dean Make Football History As many may or may not know, Highbury was a theatre when it came to all matters of sport, not only football, throughout its 93-year history (1913–2006). The grand old stage hosted football, cricket and boxing, but in terms of the beautiful game, it witnessed some of the most defining moments in footballing history. However, one of the greatest individual achievements involving Arsenal actually occurred away from the Gunners’ famous home, on the final day of the 1927/28 season, almost 100 years ago. Highbury would go on to become known as the “Home of Football” . The season proved to be nothing special for Arsenal, who were yet to embark on their “Golden Era” during the 1930s, when they lifted five league titles and two FA Cups. They finished far off from being title contenders that year. However, the man in charge was one of Arsenal’s most influential managers, Herbert Chapman, who laid the foundations for the North Londoners’ imminent future success, as well as changing the name of the closest tube station from Gillespie Road to Arsenal, amongst a number of revolutionary changes such as introducing white sleeves on the shirts during the early 1930s. His influence would eventually lead Arsenal to their first major trophy triumph in 1930 . Dixie Dean Faces Arsenal Chasing History On 5 May 1928, the Gunners travelled to Goodison Park to face Everton at their greatest, who had already been crowned league champions for the third time in their history prior to the famous game about to unfold. The official attendance was 48,715, although some accounts estimated that around 60,000 keen spectators were packed inside Goodison Park, waiting for history to be made. The Toffees featured arguably the greatest striker to ever play the game. His name was Dixie Dean, who only ever wanted to play for Everton after having been taken to watch the Merseysiders win the title during the 1914/15 season by his dad, before the football calendar was postponed for a few years due to the outbreak of the First World War. Dean was in search of breaking the English Football League record for the most goals scored in a season, which George Camsell had set with Middlesbrough not long beforehand, with 59 strikes in the Second Division before they were eventually promoted to the First Division in 1927. The only way he could set the bar was if he achieved an elusive hat-trick. The occasion also saw Arsenal legend Charlie Buchan make his final professional appearance before retiring from the game. Dean later suggested that Buchan showed little celebration of one of football’s most historic feats in the English game, perhaps feeling disappointed that Dixie’s record had overshadowed his own farewell. item.title: The Chiefs’ offense rediscovers the deep ball in Atlanta
item.description: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Leading into the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Week 10 bout with the Atlanta Falcons , quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ last deep-ball completion — a pass thrown 20 or more yards in the air — came in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders . The recipient of the throw was wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who dislocated his ankle on the play and was placed on the Reserve/Injured list. Between that play and Week 10, Mahomes completed none of his five downfield attempts. Poetically, the midseason trade for wide receiver Josh Downs was followed by Mahomes’ most prolific game of the year, with plenty of throws down the field. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Mahomes completed three of six passes 20 or more yards downfield — each to a familiar face in the receiving corps. Rookie Cyrus Allen got open on a double-move down the left sideline for a 39-yard touchdown Veteran Rashee Rice came down with a 50-yard catch on a post route in traffic Training-camp standout Andrew Armstrong hauled in a long bomb in the end zone from a scrambling Mahomes It was Mahomes’ first game with multiple deep-pass touchdowns since 2021. It felt like his confidence throwing the long ball started with intermediate passes — including an 18-yard strike to Downs at the front pylon of the end zone. The back-shoulder touchdown is a rare sight in the Chiefs’ offense, but clearly, Downs has already earned enough respect from Mahomes to step up in the pocket and rifle the attempt there. After that pass put the Chiefs up 14-6, Mahomes kept challenging Atlanta’s coverage downfield and didn’t stop until the team was coasting to a late-fourth-quarter victory; he even threw a bomb to tight end Jake Briningstool into the end zone at one point. Downs may not be the target on these deep targets all the time, but it feels as if Mahomes needed a player like Downs to help establish a rhythm — and the rest of the receivers needed a player like Downs to relieve the pressure snap to snap.

item.title: Michigan Basketball Bombards William & Mary in Record-setting Performace
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Michigan will have to update its record books. After holding a mere five-point halftime lead, defending college basketball national champion Michigan exploded in the second half for 75 points on its way to a 123-79 win over William & Mary Saturday in Ann Arbor. It was the most points by Michigan in a single half in school history, and the most points in a game by the Wolverines since 1990. It also tied for fourth place on the all-time single-game scoring output list, matching the 123 points against Illinois-Chicago in 1986. “The season is going to deliver peaks and valleys, but I think the key is us having a holistic view of we want to be better today than a week ago. Costello canned four 3-pointers and his final one snapped through the net with 5:59 left in the game to give Michigan 100 points and a 30-point lead. Also finishing in double figures were forward J.P. Estrella with 15, sophomore guard Trey McKenney with 14 and fifth-year guard Roddy Gayle Jr. with 13. item.title: CBS Inadvertently Roasts Colts CB Sauce Gardner After Embarrassing TD
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - DECEMBER 22: Sauce Gardner #1 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on prior to the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 22, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty The 2026 season has pretty much been a total nightmare for the Indianapolis Colts. The team is 2-7 entering Sunday’s game against the lowly Miami Dolphins and in the second quarter cornerback Sauce Gardner got absolutely roasted by the CBS graphic team, presumably on accident. The Dolphins employed a really nice trick play as the quarterback threw laterally to wide receiver Malik Washington and the Colts completely took the bait, moving up to try and make a tackle which allowed Jalen Tolbert to get wide open in the end zone for a very easy touchdown. The Colts player who was really responsible for the Dolphins scoring was probably either safety Cam Bynum or safety A.J. Haulcy as they both allowed Tolbert to easily get over the top, but as Haulcy ran off the field CBS flashed a graphic that said “Touchdown Sauce Gardner” which made it seem like Gardner got torched so bad on the play that he deserved credit for the touchdown. Ironically, if you watch the play Gardner is hardly even involved. He is on the far side of the field wearing No. 1 and really could not have had any sort of impact on the play even if he sprinted straight backwards towards the end zone right when the ball was snapped. You can see Gardner following Washington as he goes in motion to receive the lateral pass, but there was nothing he could have done. Still, it just speaks to the way things have gone for the Colts this season and how bad the Gardner trade looks a year later. Indianapolis traded for Gardner last November ahead of the trade deadline and gave the New York Jets two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell in the trade. Colts look foolish for the Sauce Gardner trade a year later The Colts were the inverse of what they are this season as they were 7-2 and looked to be one of the better teams in the AFC. The hope was that the trade would take them to the next level and give them a shutdown corner, but that is not how it has worked out. Gardner was one of the best corners in the NFL his first two seasons in the league but has not been the same guy in recent years. He still only has three career interceptions and does not have a pick with the Colts yet as his number of pass deflections has also gone down. That trade just looks worse and worse especially for a Colts team that is now very clearly in a state of quasi-rebuild after trading several players away in the last month. Gardner may not have deserved that graphic for the trick play from Miami, but maybe whoever pressed the wrong button on the CBS graphic crew was in some way trying to remind Colts fans just how bad an idea it was to get Gardner for that much. item.title: Why Italy will be top seeds in EURO 2028 qualifying draw
item.description: Why Italy will be top seeds in EURO 2028 qualifying draw Italy did not reach the Nations League quarter-finals, but there is still some good news, as they will be top seeds in the EURO 2028 qualifying campaign draw as one of the best third-placed teams.
